indicators.name: Taxa de desocupação (PNAD Contínua, média anual)
indicators.officialSource: IBGE – PNAD Contínua (média anual da taxa de desocupação, Brasil)
indicators.notes: Mixed vintages: 2014, 2015, 2019-2025 are from IBGE releases after the 2021 reweighting of PNAD Contínua (e.g. 2014=6.9, 2015=8.6, 2020=13.8 as cited in the Feb/2023 IBGE release); 2012, 2013, 2016, 2017, 2018 are the values as first released (original weights: 2013=7.1, 2016=11.5, 2017=12.7, 2018=12.3; the original release also had 2014=6.8, 2015=8.5, 2020=13.5). Revised values for 2013/2016-2018 were not found and may differ by ~0.1-0.2 p.p. Search snippets also cited an IBGE 'retrospectiva 2012-2024' table (Feb/2025) with a different series (7.4, 7.3, 7.0, 8.9, 11.7, 12.6, 12.2, 11.8, 13.8, 14.0, 9.6, 7.8, 6.6), possibly reweighted to Censo 2022 projections; it could not be opened (IBGE hosts blocked) so it was not used. Recommend confirming the full series in SIDRA (table 4099/6381 annual) before publication.

indicators.name: Taxa de desocupação (PME, 6 regiões metropolitanas, média anual)
indicators.officialSource: IBGE – Pesquisa Mensal de Emprego (PME), regiões metropolitanas de Recife, Salvador, Belo Horizonte, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo e Porto Alegre
indicators.notes: PME covers only 6 metropolitan regions and is NOT comparable in level with PNAD Contínua (national); e.g. 2012 PME 5.5% vs PNADC 7.4%. PME was discontinued in early 2016. 2006 annual average not found (monthly 2006 readings ranged ~8.4%-10.4%; 1st quarter 2006 average 9.9%) so it is omitted. 2003 average was 12.4% per the 2012 IBGE release.

indicators.name: Índice de Gini do rendimento domiciliar per capita
indicators.officialSource: IBGE – PNAD Contínua, Rendimento de todas as fontes (2012+); Ipea com base na PNAD anual (2007, 2011)
indicators.notes: METHODOLOGY BREAK between 2011 and 2012: 2007 and 2011 come from the old annual PNAD as computed by Ipea (2007=0.552 from Ipea Comunicado n.9; 2011=0.527 announced by Ipea in Sep/2012) and are not level-comparable with the PNAD Contínua series (2012+), which runs higher. 2006, 2008, 2009 omitted (no consistent source found; an Ipea note gave 2008=0.544 excluding rural North, not used). 2013, 2014, 2017 omitted: revised PNADC values not confirmed (originally released 2017 figure was 0.549, pre-reweighting vintage, not used). 2012-2015 trend described by IBGE as declining, 2016-2018 rising.

indicators.name: População em extrema pobreza (linha US$ 2,15/dia PPC 2017)
indicators.officialSource: IBGE – Síntese de Indicadores Sociais (SIS), com base na PNAD Contínua; linha do Banco Mundial de US$ 2,15/dia PPC 2017
indicators.notes: Single line: World Bank US$ 2.15/day (2017 PPP), as used by SIS 2023-2025 editions (SIS 2025 explicitly kept this line despite the June/2025 World Bank update). Values from SIS 2024/2025 vintages. 2013-2020 not found in the same vintage; an earlier SIS edition (2022 vintage) reported 2014=5.2% as the series low, but that vintage gave 2022=5.6% vs 5.9% in later editions, so 2014 was not mixed in. No pre-2012 values (different survey/line). Without social benefits, extreme poverty in 2024 would be ~10% per SIS 2025.

indicators.name: Aumento real do salário mínimo
indicators.officialSource: DIEESE – Notas Técnicas sobre o salário mínimo (Tabela 'Reajuste do Salário Mínimo'), reajuste nominal deflacionado pelo INPC
indicators.notes: DIEESE methodology. 2020: two adjustments (Jan R$1.039, -0.36% real; Feb R$1.045, +0.39% real); annual value 0.03% is the compounded combination computed here from the two DIEESE rows. 2022 omitted: R$1.100->R$1.212 (+10.18% nominal) was reported as having no real gain (DIEESE NT 265 'sem aumento real'), but DIEESE's exact figure was not seen. 2023: Jan/2023 R$1.302 real +1.41% (DIEESE); the May/2023 raise to R$1.320 (DIEESE: -1.01% real relative to Jan basis) is captured in 2024, which DIEESE measures Jan/2023 R$1.302 -> Jan/2024 R$1.412 (+8.45% nominal, +4.69% real). 2025: DIEESE +2.61% using full-year 2024 INPC. 2026: R$1.621 (+6.79% nominal = INPC 4.18% Dec/24-Nov/25 + 2.5% capped real gain under Lei 15.077/2024); 2.5% is the ex-ante real gain built into the formula, DIEESE's ex-post figure may differ slightly. Reajustes before 2010 occurred in April/March/February, not January. 2012 figure is DIEESE's (7.59%); some press cited 9.2% using another base.
